key_insight: The paper shows that real-time, time-domain observables can reveal resonance properties in lattice-gauge-theory scattering, making resonant dynamics more accessible to quantum simulation.
engineering_relevance: It provides a benchmark workflow for early fault-tolerant quantum hardware by mapping a physically meaningful scattering problem to measurable circuits with manageable gate scaling.
method: Exact diagonalization of pure SU(3) lattice gauge theory on a line-of-plaquettes to identify glueball scattering and resonance structure
Construction of time-domain observables designed to extract resonance information from quantum simulations
Toy-model validation plus a hardware-oriented Trotterized implementation on Quantinuum H2-2
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a 14-plaquette chain encoded in 28 qubits, with the optimized Trotterized circuit requiring about 25n entangling gates for n Trotter steps.
watch_item: The approach is still limited by near-term noise and by the fact that the most realistic resonance extraction likely needs deeper, error-mitigated or fault-tolerant circuits.
paper_title: Time-Domain Observables for Resonant Scattering in Quantum Simulations of Lattice Gauge Theory
